text: I’m a computational chemist with a passion for using machine learning and first-principles simulations to solve real-world problems in materials science and drug design. My journey from physics to chemistry to AI for science reflects my belief that interdisciplinary thinking is essential for breakthrough discoveries.

title: Research
text:
Northwestern University, 2025
Rigorous validation of high-accuracy machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for pristine and defected MoS₂/ionic-liquid ion gels. Key contributions:

DFT-accurate molecular dynamics simulations at long timescales
Integration of on-the-fly charge-equilibration schemes with MLIPs
Green–Kubo calculations for electronic conductivity

Methods: VASP, ASE, MACE, NequIP, PyTorch




Northwestern University, 2025
Large-scale study of electron transport in solution-processed BBL films, with focus on charge transport mechanisms.

DFT parametrization of hopping transport models
Gaussian site-energy distributions from MD snapshots
Distance-dependent electronic couplings (300+ configurations)

Methods: DFT, kinetic Monte Carlo, MD analysis

title: Research
text:
Past Projects

Helicases & DNA Mechanics
First-principles MD simulations of double-stranded DNA under external forces, modeling enzymatic helicase action at the quantum mechanical level. Validated experimental DNA separation forces.


Organic Solar Cells (Bachelor’s Thesis)
DFT and TD-DFT analysis of fullerene-free organic solar cell polymers, demonstrating the potential of fullerene-free designs for enhanced efficiency.

title: Angel Ivan Rodriguez-León
text:
I’m a PhD candidate in Chemistry at Northwestern University, working on computational tools to understand charge transport in complex materials. My research sits at the intersection of machine learning, quantum chemistry, and molecular dynamics simulations.
My work is motivated by a fundamental challenge: how can we design energy-efficient materials from the atomistic level up? I focus on machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and molecular simulations for mixed ionic-electronic materials relevant to neuromorphic computing—devices that mimic biological neurons by coupling ion and electron transport.



ML Interatomic Potentials for MoS₂ ion gels with on-the-fly charge equilibration
Electron Transport in organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (BBL films)
First-Principles MD Simulations for biomolecular systems and drug delivery





Prof. Monica Olvera de la Cruz — Northwestern University
Prof. Maria K. Chan — Argonne National Laboratory (Visiting Student, 2025-2026)
